ma_valley_extension.blurb: A small cluster of boulders on Cape Ann's North Shore, tucked within the central part of the Cavalry boulder field at Tompson Street Reservation, just a short stroll from the Valley and Alcove blocks and close to the highway. Thirteen problems, all bouldering, with the bulk landing around V4 and a few easier lines at V2 and V3, one V5 and a single V9 for the strong. At least one line is steep and around ten feet tall, starting from a small alcove. The granite here suits a quick visit added onto a larger session in the field rather than a trip on its own.

ma_devil_s_rock.blurb: A big glacial erratic in the woods of Sharon, beside the Massapoag Trail in eastern Massachusetts, with a couple of smaller boulders next to it. The main block stands roughly twenty feet tall and offers a slab, a tall vertical face and other sides, all in granite. Thirteen bouldering problems run from V1 up to the V9 range, with a modest group around V3 to V5 and a handful of hard lines at V7 and V8. Expect some moss and lichen on the stone and an uneven landing under the smaller overhanging block. The short walk in makes it an easy evening stop.

ma_nose_boulder_the.blurb: The largest block in the pine-covered Trees section of Gilbert Hills in Foxborough, southeast of Boston. Crack problems wrap both sides of a blunt central bulge, which gives the boulder its name. Thirteen bouldering problems here, most of them easy to moderate, from V0 through V2, with a few in the V4 and V5 range and a couple of hard ones at V7 and V8. The rock in the Trees is somewhat grainier than elsewhere in the forest, and the hillside setting makes for a pleasant mileage day alongside the neighbouring boulders. Granite throughout.

ma_goat_rock.blurb: A band of granite cliff in Gilbert Hills, Foxborough, standing about twenty to forty feet high and broken by varied features including a large detached block. The terrain runs from slab to steep overhang. Thirteen bouldering problems, with the largest share between V0 and V2, a middle group at V4 and V5, and one harder line at V6. A few lines are tall, so pads and spotters matter. It lies a short walk from the High Rock lot and pairs well with the nearby Trees boulders.

ma_bates_boulder_aka_fairy_rock.blurb: A modest granite boulder in Wellesley, within the wooded Boulder Brook Reservation, and the largest of the climbing spots there. The size is modest, with faces climbed on the north, east and west sides, and the rock gets mixed reviews for quality. Thirteen bouldering problems, nearly all easy: V0 through V3, with one V6 traverse for the stronger visitor. The shade of big trees keeps it cool and uncrowded, which suits beginners, kids and warm-up sessions. Do not expect a destination; it is best treated as a short stop for a few quick problems.

ma_hermit_s_cave.blurb: A low cave-like boulder in the wooded Hammond Pond area of Newton, west of Boston, reached by a trail that heads left of Pusherman Wall. Thirteen bouldering problems gather here, including the classic roof lines and nearby cracks that climb up beside the cave. Grades span the full range: a few V0 to V1 cracks, some mid-level problems at V4 and V5, and a pair of hard lines at V8. The cave itself has an angled, two-tiered top. It is a popular stop in the Temple Area, which holds a mix of technical vertical walls and steep overhangs.

ma_atlantis_boulder_2.blurb: The largest group of problems in the Backshore Boulders, a seaside strip of granite blocks along Atlantic Road in Gloucester on Cape Ann, opposite the oceanfront inn. Thirteen bouldering problems from V1 to V7, concentrated in the V3 to V6 range, so it appeals most to climbers already comfortable on moderate and hard boulders. A long traverse on the block is the best-regarded line at the area. The coastal setting is scenic, and some nearby boulders in the same stretch see a shorter season because of high water.

ma_tarr_trail_boulders_2.blurb: A small boulderfield in Dogtown, the large wooded tract between Gloucester and Rockport on Cape Ann, found on the left a handful of minutes along the trail. Twelve bouldering problems on the glacial granite erratics that characterise Dogtown, all in a fairly tight band: four at V3, five at V4, one V5 and two at V6. That makes it a good fit for climbers working in the middle grades. Trails in the woods are poorly marked, so bring a map or GPS rather than relying on memory.
